plain: A public office in early America that lent money to citizens.

webster.text: In America, a public office in which loans of money are negotiated for the public, or in which the accounts of loans are kept and the interest paid to the lenders.

example.quote: Perhaps this will lead to the reason why a state government, when she was obliged to pay only about an eighth part of the loan-office certificates, should voluntarily undertake the payment of about one third part of them.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, Pennsylvania Convention, Mr. WILSON, December 1, 1787 (2d ed. 1836)
